newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on exports, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on exports, soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on export news and gains in soybeans, traders said.
But trading was quiet and the volume was thin as the wheat market Friday consolidated after a week of volatile dealings.

"Everything performed about as expected. The exports were a little supportive. I was looking for 1.2 (million tonnes) and it came in around 1.1," said Warren King, wheat analyst for Cargill Investor Services.
Many analysts estimated a wheat export number at 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes but USDA Friday pegged 1997-98 U.S. net export sales of U.S. wheat at 1.071 million tonnes.
However, old crop wheat net export sales fell in the minus column to a negative 142,000 tonnes. The old crop, 1996-97 wheat marketing year ends Saturday, May 31.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed two cents per bushel higher to one lower, with July up two at $3.60-1/2.

Gains were limited by the approach of U.S. winter wheat harvesting amid recent improvements in crop condition ratings. Also weather in France, Australia and the U.S. recently turned more conducive to wheat crop production.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures declined because most harvest activity in U.S. wheat has been centered in Texas, an important HRW producing state.
"Everything's been said this week on wheat and we'll wait and see what the weather brings next week," King said. "If wet weather in Texas continues, quality could be impacted a bit.
King said the early stages of soft red winter wheat harvesting in the U.S. Southeast indicated few problems but South Carolina wheat showed some decline in yields due to a late spring freeze.
"So far in the deep south the crop looks good," King said.
Refco Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of July, LIT America bought two million July and FIMAT Futures, Lind Waldock and E.D. and F. Man International each bought one million July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, below the 24,120 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man International bought 300 September $3.50 puts at 10-3/4 to 11 cents and sold 250 September $3.80 puts at 25-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, below the 9,441 traded Thursday.
